title: fix(options): make volatility expiry investigation source-truthful
head: 27466128e9d750e9019ca46bb466f183f6456858
body:
## Outcome

Make the existing nightly Volatility surface source-truthful and turn term structure + smile into one exact-expiry investigation, without creating a new data source, cache, pricing model, calendar, ranker, alert plane, or trade-authority path.

Exact head at publication: `6dc196326bb20477690ff85b8b0a7f47f40096be`.
Base/master reconciled immediately before publication: `c35b9a1d50ca4960c361645f0300fa9f95158a4e`.

### What changes

- Preserve **numeric zero as zero** while keeping null/string/boolean/invalid IV observations unavailable.
- Break term/history/smile series at explicit gaps instead of deleting missing rows and reconnecting a false line.
- Strictly admit ISO calendar days; this is validation only, **not** a second market-session or expiry-lifecycle calendar.
- Fail closed on duplicate term expiries, smile expiries, smile strikes, and history dates rather than arbitrarily choosing a row or inflating coverage.
- Label term changes using the actual supplied tenors (for example `7→28d`) instead of approximate `0→30d` copy.
- Use one root-keyed selected-expiry context across term and smile. Missing ATM IV remains selectable and visible.
- If the selected expiry has no supplied smile, show that exact absence; **never substitute the nearest expiry**.
- Keep smile display language honest: “Full supplied range”; proxy-skew copy no longer implies observed spot moneyness.
- Reframe `vrp` UI as the source-reported **IV − trailing realized-volatility spread**, not an earned cheap/rich, directional, or sizing verdict.
- Headline ATM IV now states that this payload does not supply its tenor.

### Owner boundaries preserved

Existing owners remain in place:
- `VolView` + `flowClientCache`: root loading and request-race guard.
- `volTypes`: payload contract.
- `svgChart`: chart geometry/hygiene.
- #686: full root-universe selector.
- #723: chart-linked options companion / heatmap.

No new endpoint, transport, source-selection service, pricing engine, market calendar, source cache, probability, ranking, signal family, watcher, or trade authority is introduced.

## Verification

- Focused native unit/integration: **36/36 PASS**.
- Whole Terminal unit suite: **415 files PASS; 6,755 passed, 4 existing TODOs, 0 failures**.
- Whole-project TypeScript: **PASS**.
- Changed volatility source/tests ESLint: **0 errors / 0 warnings**.
- Added-copy plain-language gate: **PASS**; only unrelated legacy findings remain.
- Actual branch components in isolated Chromium: **84/84 assertions PASS** across **1440 / 820 / 390 × EN / ZH**.
- Production build: **PASS** using an isolated copy-on-write sandbox with an in-root dependency tree.
- `git diff --check`: **PASS**.

The six responsive captures, synthetic fixture, source hashes, commands, and claim boundaries live in:
`terminal/docs/verification/options-volatility-investigation-r1-20261001/`

The browser run uses the actual branch components with an explicitly synthetic nightly fixture. It is **not** provider, entitlement, current-market, source-host, or production acceptance.

### Build diagnostics kept separate

Two earlier build attempts were environmental diagnostics, not source failures:
1. Turbopack refused a temporary `node_modules` symlink pointing outside the isolated worktree.
2. The webpack fallback reached an unrelated existing `node:crypto` import in untouched `lib/workspaceLayout.ts`.

Changing tactic to an isolated in-root dependency copy produced the successful normal Turbopack production build above. No unrelated infrastructure was changed.

## #686 collision reconciliation

Current #686 head inspected: `450850ec2933290d6a8e86db35e8c59cfc8843c1`.

#686 and this PR both touch `VolView.tsx`, but #686 only changes the existing `rootChoices` prop/datalist seam. A three-way merge simulation:
- **auto-merges VolView cleanly**, retaining both `rootChoices` and this PR’s `expiryChoice` / shared context;
- exits nonzero only because #686 already conflicts with current master in `ops/terminal_source_audit.production.json`.

The synthetic merged VolView was inspected and contains both capabilities. This PR does not absorb or replace #686.

## Paper / design reference

Existing editable Paper file `Terminal`, page `09 · Options · Volatility Lab`:
- V01 desktop: `UM6-0`
- V02 mobile: `URH-0`
- V03 source / missing / refresh states: `UT6-0`

Those boards use synthetic design data and are not claimed as native prototype or production proof. The Paper lane was frozen after repeated `DOCUMENT_CHANGED` while another file was active; no blind write retry was used.

## Remaining acceptance gates

This PR should remain **DRAFT** until:
- real entitled/published volatility data is proven through the native route for a covered root;
- stale / missing / root-switch behavior is proven on that native route;

Synthetic fixtures do **not** establish provider methodology, executable marks, whole-chain completeness, current market state, relative value, probability, ranking, sizing, or trade authority.

title: perf(chart): reuse pane-sync time brackets
head: 9a4cf00f6f1c894413fe0992fe242472a04bec6a
body:
## Outcome

Reduce multi-pane pan/zoom synchronization work without changing pane-sync authority, calendar semantics, edge clamping, or Lightweight Charts ownership.

`logicalAtTime()` maps a calendar instant back into one pane's logical index. During a synchronized pan, the same long-lived `AxisClock` receives alternating left/right endpoints that move only slightly from frame to frame. Before this patch every endpoint restarted a binary search through the pane's bar set.

This patch keeps two recent inverse-mapping hints per AxisClock in a WeakMap:
- one naturally tracks the left viewport edge and one the right;
- a hint is never trusted blindly;
- its fresh neighboring timestamps must still bracket the requested instant;
- if validation fails, the existing exact binary search runs unchanged;
- a mutable clock therefore remains correct;
- WeakMap lifetime follows the clock and cannot retain a retired pane.

No pane-sync operation token, chart write, time authority, data series, ChartPanel, or UI behavior changed.

## RED → GREEN

4096-bar synthetic clock, nearby next viewport after one warm conversion:

- before: **32 `msAt` probes**
- after: **8 probes**
- exact next range remains `{ from: 1700.35, to: 1950.85 }`

The regression gate allows <=10 probes so implementation details can evolve without restoring two full searches.

A second test mutates the backing timestamps in place after warming the cache. The old hint no longer brackets the target, is rejected, and the exact fallback returns the newly correct logical index.

## Verification

- hot-path + time-window + pane-sync unit contracts: **34/34 PASS**
- ESLint: PASS
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: PASS
- broad suite: **372 files / 6,017 passed / 4 todo**, with one unrelated `flagshipPine` runtime-ceiling failure under the loaded sweep
- exact `flagshipPine` isolation immediately after: **4/4 PASS in 0.5 s**
- `npm run build`: PASS on Next 16.2.9
- `git diff --check`: PASS
- protected base: `1199aba21aecb5a57c9d8bf5a5634928a9dc1b4a`

### Real browser pane-sync contract

Desktop `pane-sync-time-axis.spec.ts`: **7/7 PASS**
- manual pan with different listing dates;
- four-pane convergence across four history depths;
- wheel zoom + programmatic reset;
- no-overlap edge parking terminates;
- Sync off leaves panes independent;
- pane removal leaves no stale registration;
- mirrored crosshair still resolves each pane's own value.

## Collision control

This PR edits only:
- `terminal/lib/timeWindow.ts`
- `terminal/lib/__tests__/timeWindowHotPath.test.ts`

It does not edit `paneSync.ts`, which remains owned by open chart correctness work.

## Continuation frontier

The next smoothness work should continue from measured hot paths. CSS containment on `.chart-wrap` was explicitly rejected because it would create a containing block for fixed drawing UI, violating an existing chart contract. Gradient-line global color regrouping was also rejected because it could alter round-cap seam z-order.

title: perf(chart): pack suite memo snapshots
head: e8aebe0fa96a47ae808790ab87c32e400ea875aa
body:
## Outcome

Round 6 of the Terminal chart-smoothness program removes the dominant validation overhead from premium-suite cache hits during pan, zoom, resize, and any other overlay repaint that reuses unchanged OHLCV data.

`computeSuite()` correctly memoizes premium-suite computation, but every memo hit still walked every bar and every string-keyed field (`time/o/h/l/c/v`) before returning the cached bundle. With five active suites and 1,255 bars, a single visual frame can ask the host for multiple unchanged bundles, so this “hit” path remained an O(bars × suites) main-thread tax.

This patch preserves exact content validation while changing its representation:

- timestamps remain in an exact `Array<string | number>`;
- numeric OHLCV fields are packed into one `Float64Array` as `[o,h,l,c,v,…]`;
- comparison is unrolled and retains `Object.is` semantics;
- immutable suite-definition metadata (owned module keys and module-key signature) is cached in a `WeakMap` instead of rebuilt on every hit;
- equal payload copies still hit;
- in-place historical corrections still invalidate;
- `-0` vs `+0` remains a correction;
- `NaN` vs `NaN` remains equal;
- the bounded 32-entry LRU behavior and cached result identity are unchanged.

No chart math, suite algorithm, prim output, chart data, settings, JSX, CSS, colors, copy, coordinates, or renderer behavior changed.

## Measured cache-hit delta

Deterministic benchmark using the real all-on Structure, Trend, Pulse, RSI Ultimate, and MACD Ultimate runtime definitions over a 1,255-bar fixture. The benchmark warms all five suites, then measures 1,000 cache-hit calls per sample.

| Path | Before median | Candidate median | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Same input array | 0.123900 ms/call | 0.006494 ms/call | **94.8%** |
| Equal copied payload | 0.115402 ms/call | ~0.0065 ms/call | **~94%** |

Candidate p95 was **0.006966 ms/call**. The packed-only version measured ~0.007446 ms/call; caching immutable suite metadata removed another ~13%, after which marginal gains flattened and the implementation was frozen.

This is an implementation microbenchmark, not a production FPS claim. It targets the exact cache-hit path called by the chart overlay renderer.

## Correctness discriminator

New `suiteMemoSnapshot.test.ts` pins the semantics that a cheaper identity-only cache would break:

- a separately allocated but byte-equivalent payload returns the same cached result;
- payloads containing `NaN` and signed zero still hit when exactly equal;
- changing `-0` to `+0` invalidates;
- reassigning `NaN` to `NaN` does not invalidate;
- an in-place historical close correction invalidates and recomputes.

The existing Visual Intelligence historical-correction contract also remains green: same-length, same-last-time edits in the middle of the series cannot become stale memo hits.

## Verification

- full Terminal suite: **371 files / 6,011 passed / 4 todo**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: pass
- `npm run build`: pass on Next 16.2.9
- new memo contracts + existing correction parity: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass
- new test file ESLint: pass
- diff-aware `host.ts` lint: **0 findings on added lines**; the file retains 7 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` reports outside this patch
- exact protected base at commit: `cc0da169b16a9f975801f3628352be238357fe81`
- candidate commit: `6f1ea0a85f2e7551702f5b22524e78fabc07cf4b`

## Visual-evidence gate

`terminal/lib/indicator-canvas/host.ts` is included in the Terminal Visual Intelligence source lock, so this logic-only performance change was not allowed to bypass that gate.

Acceptance reran the real browser journeys:

- Visual Intelligence EN/ZH matrix: **30/30 passed** across desktop, tablet, and mobile
- crosshair / price-axis collision matrix: **27/27 applicable passed**, 6 intentional viewport-specific skips
- mobile new-chart right-space regression: **5/5 repeated passes**

A fresh capture changed all six PNG byte hashes, but inspection showed the chart, candles, indicators, context panel, copy, and geometry unchanged. The changed pixels were unrelated current-master/session state in the right sidebar (`Briefs`) and market-closed chrome. This PR therefore does **not** bless those unrelated pixels into the Visual Intelligence evidence packet.

The prior six crops are retained, and `EVIDENCE.yml` contains an explicit hash-only-restamp receipt plus the browser gate results. The source lock now records the candidate `host.ts` SHA-256:

`2c04d008eafc9312d64bb238d728e4ea398dd55fd5218dfc644502630dc5b02b`

The evidence contract itself is green.

## Changed paths

- `terminal/lib/indicator-canvas/host.ts`
- `terminal/lib/__tests__/suiteMemoSnapshot.test.ts`
- `terminal/docs/pr-crops/terminal-visual-intelligence/EVIDENCE.yml`

## Collision control

This slice is path-disjoint from:

- Round 1 quote scheduling (`TerminalShell`)
- Round 5 square-marker batching (`render.ts`, planner, browser contract)
- active `ChartPanel.tsx` feature/fix work

## Continuation frontier

After this slice, remaining measured dense-view costs are actual SVG reconstruction—especially gradline segments and label groups—not suite-cache validation. Those renderer paths should remain held while Round 5 owns the renderer, then be attacked only with a discriminating geometry/order contract.

Do not redo the lifecycle leak audit, cold-start timeframe repair, resize coalescing, single-flight quote lane, pane-sync cursor coalescing, tooltip-follow scheduling, histogram batching, phase-ribbon batching, or this exact memo snapshot optimization.

title: fix(discover): make Flow Leaders historical snapshot scannable

body:
## Outcome

Polish the restored Discover → Leaders surface so the recovered historical board is usable instead of becoming a 133-row wall of machine-like output.

This is a **presentation-only** follow-up to #659 / #666. It does not alter Flow Leaders data, scoring, ordering, source law, or authority.

## What changes

- Show the first **12** rows of the selected board by default.
- Add an explicit **Show all N / Show top 12** control over the same sorted array.
- Keep that control in the board toolbar, so expanding 133 rows does not move the collapse action thousands of pixels below the viewport.
- Reset expansion when switching between Flow Leadership and Washout Turn.
- Separate board membership from universe coverage:
  - before: `top 133 of 368`
  - after: `Showing 12 of 133 · 368-name universe`
- On the stale historical snapshot, missing recurrence reads **historical** rather than **accruing**.
- Replace the valid-empty “updates after tonight's build” sentence with **No qualifying names in this snapshot**.
- Replace the enormous `Sources: AAL, AAPL, ...` ticker dump with a concise coverage line: **Tape-signed coverage: N names.**
- Replace machine-style source mechanics (`sessions 145/5`, raw `FL-R3` note, duplicate build timestamp) with `145 sessions of history` and a plain confidence sentence.

No row is hidden permanently; expansion exposes every delivered row without re-filtering or re-ranking.

The Macro producer is still Macro #7399 at exact head `dd47741bebb102e94e4f6379551d1fc8ec58ea37`. Its projection logic is proven, but hosted CI correctly found that `engine/prophet_integrity.py` becomes macro-api request-cached while missing from the deploy restart law. That shared `app/deploy/update.sh` repair belongs to incumbent Macro #6872, which is itself sequenced behind #7390.

### Capability

The surface deliberately does **not** create a score, rank, win-rate, backtest, benchmark, portfolio return, option P&L, alpha, or trade authority.

- Option result stays unavailable when canonical evidence is null.
- Benchmark/excess remains unavailable unless the producer explicitly supplies valid benchmark evidence.
- `NO_ENTRY` is a no-position terminal outcome and cannot carry stock/option result.

The client schema adapter fails closed on cross-field inconsistencies: duplicate IDs, hidden nulls, impossible no-entry P&L, count mismatches, invalid quarantine/effective totals, raw-return arithmetic mismatches, unsupported benchmark claims, and inconsistent source freshness.

The first hosted run on `46e1be09...` found one real integration issue in the Python source-audit gate: placing the synthetic fixture under `terminal/public/data` changed the production runtime-subtree tree hash.

Same-carrier repair `0655c923...` moves that synthetic-only fixture to `terminal/test-fixtures/prophet_perf_fixture.json` and updates the server fixture path. It deliberately does **not** widen `ops/terminal_source_audit.production.json`.

title: Make launchd transcript state writes safe on offloaded fund storage
head: 1f8c4e77b3c4d04c36ec844743cd752e13a1d8e1
body:
## Incident follow-up

The 2026-09-19 Earnings Wire recovery proved a second, independent production defect after the DefeatBeta URL repair: on the M1 launchd owner, `fund-src` is symlinked to the external STORAGE volume. The Python collector can write that state, but launchd shell `touch`/`mv` calls against the same paths fail with `Operation not permitted`.

Observed after the successful 29,570-body transcript publication:
- `touch .../.role_inference_v2_ok: Operation not permitted`
- `mv .../_tx_index.json: Operation not permitted`
- revision-candidate → applied-revision `mv` denied, so the refresh stamp could not advance

The public archive was already safely published, but leaving this unfixed would make the next nightly treat the same 2.275 GB provider revision as unapplied and redo the backfill, while the legacy fund join index remained stale.

## Change

- add a tiny stdlib `ingest/fund_state_ops.py` filesystem helper
- copy validated `/tmp` index bytes into a temporary file on the destination filesystem, fsync, then atomically replace
- route the existing legacy-index replacement, revision-marker promotion, role-repair stamp and refresh stamp through the lane's already-authorized Python process
- keep every existing path/marker/state owner unchanged; no new state plane or publication path

## Proof

- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_fund_state_ops.py` → 4 passed on the production M1
- `bash -n ops/nightly_fund.sh` → pass
- `git diff --check` → pass
- the incident was manually reconciled after the owning launchd run exited: local index now 3,671 symbols / 29,570 pairs, applied/cache revisions both `etag:1758cdc…`, and both existing stamps advanced.

This PR is durability hardening only; it does not rerun or duplicate the already-completed transcript publication.

title: fix(briefs): centralize scheduling and make delivery explicit
head: bc539d62f68ddea1aff748786396ee78f754f062
body:
## Outcome

Replace the confusing recurring-Briefs entry points with one coherent management surface.

The old UI said “Send me a brief…” without saying where anything was sent and placed scheduling controls inside primary watchlist/thesis workflows. This redesign makes the contract explicit:

**Delivery: Terminal → Alerts → Briefs. Email and push are not available yet.**

Alerts remains the default `/alerts` surface. Briefs is a sibling surface reached deliberately from Alerts or directly at `/alerts#briefs`; the two are not stacked into one long page.

## Product flow

Inside Alerts → Briefs a signed-in user can:

- choose an owned active thesis or watchlist;
- choose **After each US close** or **Every Saturday**;
- add the schedule;
- see the target name, human cadence and Scheduled/Paused state;
- pause/resume existing schedules;
- read delivered or honest-miss briefs in the same place they were scheduled.

The legacy contextual `BriefSubscribeControls` compatibility component is intentionally inert: it renders nothing and performs no subscription reads/writes. Permanent watchlist/thesis chrome is no longer a Briefs-management plane.

## Scope

- centralized schedule creation + management inside Alerts → Briefs
- separate Alerts/Briefs page surfaces so Briefs does not enlarge the default Alerts composition
- direct `/alerts#briefs` deep link
- owner-scoped target-name projection; raw UUIDs are not human labels
- delivered rows use human cadence, never raw cadence slugs
- truthful empty/read-unavailable states
- Macro watchlist bodies accept `version_or_asof: null`; thesis versions remain required
- EN/ZH parity and desktop/mobile proof
- no new scheduler, schema, queue, signal engine, email, push, SMS, or second notification plane

## Product-integrity rulings

The schema defines `brief_deliveries.subscription_id ... on delete cascade`. A casual **Remove schedule** control would erase delivered Brief history. This PR therefore exposes **pause/resume**, not destructive deletion, until there is an explicit history-deletion contract and confirmation flow.

The contextual scheduler is also fail-closed: its compatibility component is inert. New schedules originate only from the central Briefs surface.

## Dependency / HOLD

This PR remains **DRAFT / HOLD** for production activation.

The canonical Macro producer is now implemented and repaired on the existing daily/weekly owners:
- producer path merged through Macro #7106
- privacy/cadence/read-truth repair merged through #7414
- incumbent Supabase runtime-secret wiring merged through #7474

However `RECURRING_BRIEFS_ENABLE` remains intentionally off. Do not merge/activate this user-facing scheduling surface merely because source CI is green. Production release still owes the real path:

signed-in schedule → scheduled canonical owner run → `brief_deliveries` row → Terminal `/alerts#briefs` visible result.

The live cleanup path is separate: Terminal #658 already removed the watchlist card + Settings row, and #677 removes the remaining old Thesis Workspace scheduler.

## Proof on current semantic head

Current head: `bc539d62f68ddea1aff748786396ee78f754f062`

Local proof:
- affected evidence + Briefs Vitest: 59/59
- TypeScript: clean
- Briefs desktop/mobile Playwright: 12/12
- default Alerts crop regressions that previously overflowed: 6/6 with 0px overflow
- B-F11-7 dark EN/ZH desktop/mobile crops retained on the central Briefs surface
- contextual scheduler source contains no subscription endpoint, POST/PATCH action or rendered control
- plain-language gate: new Alerts/Briefs surface copy routed through an EN/ZH picker; local enforcement has zero blocking findings
- `git diff --check`: clean

Hosted CI for this exact head is the remaining repository integration proof.
